title: Enterprise Agents Have a Structure Problem - Ishita Daga, Tesla
talk_summary: Ishita Daga argues enterprise data agents fail mainly from ambiguity over source-of-truth, stale context, and unmodeled user/team preferences, not from insufficient model size. She proposes a source hierarchy, a context lifecycle with event logging and evaluation, and preference-aware routing, while admitting preference remains unsolved.

takeaways.what_they_do: They rank knowledge sources from curated semantic definitions to canonical queries to a messy database graph, and have the agent search in that order.
takeaways.evidence_quote: start from the cleanest to the messiest or the most dynamic one.

takeaways.what_they_do: They log every correction or definition change as an event, then use it to update context and evaluate the agent.
takeaways.evidence_quote: All of these events need to be captured, logged, and used to update your data agent context.

takeaways.what_they_do: They build automated evals from recent questions and actual answers to compare new agent answers.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can create an automated evaluation where you see all the questions that have been asked in the last couple of days and the actual answers

takeaways.what_they_do: They propose routing the agent to the right metric/definition based on the team or individual using it, rather than one global memory.
takeaways.evidence_quote: route the agent to the right metric based on who

takeaways.what_they_do: They recommend building curated semantic definitions and canonical queries first, and deferring the expensive database graph.
takeaways.evidence_quote: start adding the first and the second layer first.

takeaways.what_they_do: They require context sources to be live, reviewed, and always updated rather than stale copied docs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: data sources that are going to be always updated, would be reviewed and well curated
